finding.title: Add Locale('he') coverage for LearningScreen's error-state branches — test suite cannot catch AppErrorView's fully-hardcoded English strings

evidence.quote:
testWidgets(
    'shows AppErrorView with "Something went wrong" when curricula stream errors',
testWidgets('daily tasks error: AppErrorView shown inside tasks section', (

finding.why: LearningScreen routes both its curricula-load error and daily-tasks-load error through AppErrorView. I read app_error_view.dart in full: every string in it ('Something went wrong', 'No connection', 'Invalid data', 'Access denied', 'Retry', 'Report this issue', the snackbar text) is a raw Dart string literal — zero AppLocalizations/l10n calls anywhere in the file. This screen is the app's home screen and a churn HOTSPOT; the test suite does have a working Locale('he') mechanism (tests 17/18 exercise it for empty/data states) but never applies it to either error-state test, so nothing in this suite would fail if a Hebrew-speaking user hits any network/permission/not-found/internal error anywhere AppErrorView is used and sees raw English text — a real, live i18n defect in an RTL app that ships EN/HE parity as a named requirement.
finding.recommendation: Add a Locale('he') variant of the curricula-error and daily-tasks-error tests asserting the rendered text is NOT the literal English strings (this should fail today, proving the gap per TQ-8's red-first-regression convention). File the underlying fix separately: app_error_view.dart's _ErrorConfig strings need to route through AppLocalizations/ARB keys.
acceptance_criteria: New testWidgets(..., locale: Locale('he')) variant for the curricula-error and daily-tasks-error paths exists and currently fails against app_error_view.dart as written
Once app_error_view.dart is localized (separate fix), the new Hebrew-locale tests assert the Hebrew string and assert find.text('Something went wrong') findsNothing under Locale('he')
